problems.issueText: Upstream issue #13926: the Python domain treats the ':canonical:' option of the 'py:type' directive incorrectly — it notes the canonical name as an aliased index object, producing wrong index entries; for py:type the canonical option names the true TypeVar and must not create a separate index object. Fix in sphinx/domains/python/ so py:type + canonical stops producing the wrong index object; other python object types keep current handling. Reproduce, fix, verify via a tiny sample.

Upstream issue #13328: PEP 695 type-alias syntax is not handled by the Python domain — new-style `type X = ...` declarations produce missing or wrong py-domain entries and annotations, unlike legacy assignments. Fix sphinx/domains/python/ handling so PEP 695 aliases resolve like comparable alias forms; keep legacy behavior intact. Reproduce, fix, verify via a tiny sample.

Upstream issue #13762 (RETAINED NEGATIVE — clean re-run produced pytest_exit 2 twice; see lesson.bench-oracle-isolation). This problem is kept in the set as an explicit negative control: the runner must REFUSE admission for retained-negative problems.
